entities.evidence: Genesis 5 records the 930-year lifespan of Adam, the father of Seth. The source tag identifies the same person.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with יְמֵי in כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם, “all the days of Adam.” The numerical predicate gives the total length of his life as nine hundred and thirty years.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: to amount to a stated total

analysis.evidence: כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם means “all the days of Adam.” The verse gives their combined duration as 930 years, so כָּל refers to his whole lifespan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם, יְמֵי is the construct form governed by כָּל and completed by אָדָם, giving “all the days of Adam.” The clause אֲשֶׁר חַי (“that he lived”) and the total of 930 years identify those days as his lifespan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (pl.) days of a life, a reign or an age

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם, “all the days of Adam,” the name identifies whose lifespan is counted. The verse gives his age as 930 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם אֲשֶׁר חַי, “all the days of Adam that he lived,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause describing the days. Adam is the understood subject of חַי.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם אֲשֶׁר חַי, “all the days that Adam lived,” חַי is the verb of the relative clause, with Adam as its subject. The verse totals those days at 930 years and closes with וַיָּמֹת, “and he died.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular
analysis.sense: to live for a span of time

analysis.evidence: תְּשַׁע counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. Its construct form gives תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה ‘nine hundred years’, to which וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה adds thirty years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular cardinal numeral in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה means “nine hundred years.” תְּשַׁע counts the hundreds, and וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה adds thirty years, giving Adam a lifespan of 930 years.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: In תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, “nine hundred years,” the singular שָׁנָה gives the unit of the count. כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם אֲשֶׁר חַי identifies what is counted as the span of Adam’s life.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה adds thirty years to תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה ‘nine hundred years’, giving Adam a lifespan of 930 years.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וּ ‘and’ + cardinal numeral, common gender, plural, absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה, “and thirty years,” the marked noun gives the unit for the final thirty years of Adam’s 930-year lifespan. The verse identifies the total as כָּל יְמֵי אָדָם אֲשֶׁר חַי, “all the days that Adam lived.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After giving Adam’s lifespan as 930 years, the verse closes with וַיָּמֹת. Adam is the subject, and the verb records his death.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life
